meta.title:
Plate Thickness Optimization and
Vibration Analysis of Platform Plate Supporting Dust Suppression Cannon

summary: This project focuses on optimizing the thickness of a platform plate supporting a dust suppression cannon using finite element analysis. The goal was to reduce material usage while ensuring structural safety under a 600–700 kg load and high-speed operating conditions. The optimized design achieves significant weight reduction without compromising performance or safety.

challenge.description: The existing platform plate had a thickness of 10 mm, resulting in higher material usage and cost. The challenge was to reduce the thickness while ensuring it could safely support a 600–700 kg operational load. Additionally, the system had to maintain structural integrity under vibration at 2880 RPM and avoid resonance conditions that could lead to failure or excessive deflection.

methodology.title: Geometry & Material Definition
methodology.description: A 3D model of the platform plate was created in ANSYS and assigned S-275 structural steel properties, including elastic modulus, density, and Poisson’s ratio.

methodology.title: Static Structural Analysis
methodology.description: Load conditions of 600–700 kg were applied on the platform with fixed supports at mounting points. Stress and deformation were evaluated for thickness variations from 10 mm to 5 mm.

methodology.title: Modal & Vibration Analysis
methodology.description: Modal analysis was performed to determine natural frequencies of the structure. Harmonic analysis at 2880 RPM excitation frequency was conducted to ensure no resonance conditions occurred.

methodology.title: Thickness Optimization
methodology.description: Iterative comparison of results for thicknesses from 10 mm to 5 mm was performed to identify the minimum safe thickness with acceptable stress and deformation levels.

impact.label: MATERIAL REDUCTION
impact.description: Plate thickness successfully reduced from 10 mm to 5 mm, significantly lowering material usage and cost.

impact.label: MAXIMUM STRESS CONTROLLED
impact.description: Stress levels remained low and well within allowable limits for S-275 structural steel under all tested conditions.

impact.label: RESONANCE RISK
impact.description: No resonance was observed between operating frequency and natural frequencies, ensuring safe dynamic performance.
